title: Richard Sterban, Oak Ridge Boys Bass Singer Who Helped Make ‘Elvira’ a Hit, Dies at 83
summary: Known for his signature "oom poppa, mow mow" bass line on "Elvira," Sterban had 17 No. 1s on the Hot Country Songs chart with The Oak Ridge Boys, plus two top 40 hits on the all-genre Hot 100.
body: Richard Sterban, the bass vocalist behind the “oom poppa, mow mow” hook on one of The Oak Ridge Boys ‘ biggest hits, “Elvira,” and whose career launched as a backing singer for Elvis Presley , died on Saturday (Nov. 14). He was 83. Related Gone But Not Forgotten: Musicians We Lost in 2026 The Oak Ridge Boys’ Top 10 Billboard Hot Country Songs Hits The Oak Ridge Boys Member Richard Sterban Diagnosed With Pancreatic Cancer Sterban passed away due to complications from bronchitis and pneumonia in Hendersonville, Tenn., his family shared. He died after a long battle with cancer, and after retiring from touring last year. “We appreciate all of your love, support, and prayers,” the Sterban family said in a statement released on Saturday. “Please continue to lift us up in this difficult time. We find comfort knowing that he is currently face to face with Jesus.” Sterban, a member of The Oak Ridge Boys for more than 50 years with Duane Allen, William Lee Golden and the late Joe Bonsall, revealed a pancreatic cancer diagnosis in September 2025 , saying at the time that he was “under the care of the best cancer…

title: Karol G Surprises Mexico City Fans With Thalía as Special Guest: ‘The First Person I Wanted to Be’
summary: The Nov. 13 show at the GNP Seguros Stadiums marked the first performance of the Mexican pop icon in Mexico City.
body: Karol G gave her fans a huge surprise on Friday (Nov. 13) during the first of her three nights at the Estadio GNP Seguros in Mexico City, inviting Thalia to join her on stage for a special performance. The Mexican superstar then took to the stage wearing a replica of her iconic guitar-shaped bustier from her “Amor a la Mexicana” era — one of the most famous outfits in Latin pop culture. summary: No SD card, no problem.
body: Credit: Pankil Shah / Android Authority My Galaxy S26 only has 256GB of internal storage, and there’s no SD card slot to expand it. So yes, storage is a constant struggle for me, especially with a camera this good that I just can’t stop using. But I wasn’t about to sacrifice my precious photos to free up space, so I went looking for other ways to do it. I went through forgotten apps, bloated caches, offline downloads, and old files I didn’t need anymore. It helped free up 36GB of storage, and more importantly, it wasn’t anywhere near as tedious as I kept assuming it would be.

title: Google gets ready to kill off Pixel 10 Magic Cue in favor of Proactive Assistance
summary: Google appears to be preparing to pull the plug on Magic Cue by the end of 2027.
body: TL;DR Magic Cue launched on Pixel 10 phones, offering to find useful info in your apps and bring it to your attention. Proactive Assistance debuted with the Pixel 11 series, working quite similarly to Magic Cue, and we’ve been wondering if it’s meant to replace it. New text strings now highlight Google’s plans to move Magic Cue users to Proactive Assistance by the end of 2027. Google first introduced Proactive Assistance with the Pixel 11 series this year, and now it looks like the company is getting ready to fully replace Magic Cue with its new system — eventually. APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship. Magic Cue debuted with Pixel 10 phones, attempting to proactively surface information from apps around your phone when you need it most. But then when we got Proactive Assistance on the Pixel 11 , it largely just felt like more of the same. We even looked at some evidence that seemed to support the idea that Proactive Assistance might be designed as a replacement for Magic Cue .

title: Google Maps, Spotify, and more are coming to Xiaomi 18 Pro’s rear display
summary: Xiaomi wants you to spend more time looking at your phone's back.
body: TL;DR Xiaomi is making the rear display on its upcoming 18 Pro series more useful with new app integrations. Google Maps, Spotify, and YouTube Music will work on the rear screen, letting you check directions and control music. You can also create simple apps using generative AI and access them directly on the rear display. A second screen on the back of a smartphone is a pretty cool idea, but there’s only so much excitement in checking notifications or looking at the time. I’ve always felt that if a phone has an extra display, it should let you do things without constantly turning to the main screen. That’s partly why the Xiaomi 17 Pro series caught my attention. The small display next to the rear cameras looked interesting, but unfortunately, the phones never reached global markets.

title: Google Wallet now lets Gemini analyze your spending and suggest ways to save
summary: Gemini now knows where your money goes, even when you don't.
body: TL;DR Google Wallet is now integrating with Gemini’s Personal Intelligence to help you better understand your finances. You can ask Gemini to analyze spending, find forgotten subscriptions, and suggest ways to save money. The optional, read-only integration is rolling out in the US across Android, iOS, and the web. Keeping track of where your money goes every month isn’t always easy, especially when you’re juggling multiple bank accounts, credit cards, and subscriptions. Google now wants Gemini to help you make sense of your spending without sifting through all those transactions yourself. As we first reported back in September , Google is now bringing Wallet integration to Gemini’s Personal Intelligence feature. For context, Personal Intelligence already connects Gemini to services like Gmail, YouTube , and Photos to provide more personalized answers. With Wallet joining that list, Gemini can now help you understand your spending habits and manage your budget.

title: Google’s November Pixel update is leaving screensavers stuck at full brightness
summary: The update seemingly broke low-light mode for screensavers.
body: TL;DR Pixel users are reporting that their screensavers’ low-light mode has stopped working properly after Google’s November update. Affected users say their screensavers remain unusually bright at night, with some reporting that manually lowering the brightness only helps temporarily. The issue doesn’t appear to be widespread, and there’s no confirmed fix yet. Google’s big November update seems to have broken a lot of features , and Pixel’s low-light mode for screensavers is the latest casualty. Several Pixel users have taken to platforms like Reddit and the Google Support forum to report that their phones’ screensavers aren’t dimming while charging at night. Naturally, this is leaving users with unusually bright bedrooms. For reference, the feature, which can be accessed via Settings > Display & touch > Screen saver, lets you select a built-in screensaver that appears while your device is charging. It can be set to only show while charging, while upright and charging, or only while wirelessly charging. Considering that a lot of us charge our phones overnight, the accompanying low-light mode is a nifty addition that ensures screensavers adjust to the surrounding lightin…

title: Android Auto’s music controls are still skipping two songs with one press
summary: One button press, two skipped songs, and no fix in sight.
body: TL;DR Android Auto users are reporting that a single press of their steering-wheel media controls skips two songs instead of one. Initially reported by Toyota RAV4 owners earlier this year, the issue is now being reported with other vehicles and aftermarket stereos. Google support has contacted affected users and escalated recent complaints to the Android Auto team, but there’s no confirmed fix. Steering-wheel buttons are supposed to make controlling music easier while driving, but some Android Auto users are finding that a single press can send their playlists two songs forward or backward. It’s a frustrating problem that has been around for months, and fresh complaints suggest it isn’t going away anytime soon. The issue first gained attention earlier this year , when owners of the 2026 Toyota RAV4 reported that pressing the next or previous button on their steering wheels registered two commands instead of one. The behavior affected multiple music apps, including Spotify and YouTube Music, across wired and wireless connections.

title: Peanuts Native brings 12 Switch games to Android without an emulator layer
summary: The open-source translation layer builds on BananaNative, and supports dual-screen Android handhelds.
body: Credit: AYN TL;DR Peanuts Native is a new open-source fork of BananaNative that converts 12 Nintendo Switch games into standalone Android apps without a traditional emulator layer. Created by the developer behind Eden Duo, it supports dual-screen Android handhelds like the AYN Thor by rendering interactive companion overlays with haptic feedback on the bottom display. Converting legally dumped game files takes five to 40 minutes on-device and requires Android 13 or later, at least 12GB of RAM, and a Snapdragon GPU with Vulkan 1.3 support. It’s an exciting time to be an Android emulation fan. Not only is the emulation scene moving quickly lately, but native recompilation projects are also speeding up, letting you bypass the emulator layer to run console titles “natively” on Android. Nintendo Switch 2 emulators have recently landed on various platforms, including Android, and projects like BananaNative have inspired other devs to port console titles like The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake to Android within a week of release! title: After BP monitoring smartwatches, HUAWEI reveals its first continuous glucose monitor
summary: Data from the CGM can also be viewed directly on a HUAWEI smartwatch.
body: Credit: Weibo / Huawei TL;DR HUAWEI has revealed a continuous glucose monitor in China. HUAWEI Sence G1 is the company’s first-ever Class III medical device. HUAWEI hasn’t shared details about availability but said it has been in development for over three years. HUAWEI may have been nearly wiped out of international markets by sanctions imposed on it during the first tenure of US President Donald Trump, but it remains at the top of China’s leaderboard. Along with its innovations across slab phones, foldables , and laptops —including laptops with foldable screens —HUAWEI also offers a broad range of wearables, including ones that monitor blood pressure . So far, the lineup has only comprised smartwatches and fitness bands, but HUAWEI is now adding a health-centric utility in the form of a glucose monitor. The HUAWEI Sence G1 is the company’s first continuous glucose monitor (CGM). The device works alongside other HUAWEI products, allowing users to view glucose levels on their phones, a smartwatch, or a HUAWEI fitness band. Besides monitoring a user’s glucose levels, the CGM will also alert them in case of any unusual spikes or dips.

title: Motorola Signature 27 could have a downgraded 5,500mAh battery in some markets (Update)
summary: It looks like Motorola's flagship phone won't have a 7,000mAh battery everywhere.
body: Credit: Stephen Radochia / Android Authority TL;DR A regulatory filing has revealed that the Motorola Signature 27 is available in two models, with each having a different battery capacity. The standard phone has a rated capacity of 6,790mAh, while the downgraded model has a rated capacity of 5,350mAh. It’s not clear which countries will receive the Signature 27 with a smaller battery. Update: November 13, 2026 (6:26 AM ET): It looks like Motorola was indeed planning to offer a Signature 27 with a 5,500mAh battery in some markets. The phone’s product page mentioned a smaller battery in markets like Germany and the UK (see first screenshot below), but this has subsequently been updated to only mention a 7,000mAh battery. In fact, Google still mentions a 5,500mAh battery, as seen in the second image below. We’ve asked Motorola for clarity regarding this battery situation and will update our article accordingly. Here’s hoping the Signature 27 is available with a 7,000mAh battery in all markets.

title: 6 reasons I’d still buy the Galaxy S26 Ultra instead of the Motorola Signature 27
summary: The Motorola Signature 27 looks impressive, but Samsung's S26 Ultra still has a few tricks up its sleeve.
body: Credit: Stephen Radochia / Android Authority On paper, the Motorola Signature 27 looks like an almost unbeatable flagship. With a massive 7,000mAh silicon-carbon battery, an eye-catching 200MP telephoto camera, and a newer 2nm Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset, Motorola has built an uncompromising spec-sheet juggernaut. Yet, numbers in a vacuum do not make a flagship a must-buy. Despite Motorola’s aggressive leap into the ultra-premium tier, there are good reasons to continue leaning towards the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra as a potentially smarter, more cohesive purchase. Here are six reasons you should pick Samsung’s flagship over Motorola’s latest challenger.

title: Pixel’s November update is breaking AOD, lock screen, and notifications for some users
summary: Bugs introduced with the November 2026 update continue to pile up for Pixel owners.
body: Credit: Rita El Khoury / Android Authority TL;DR Pixel users are reporting several sporadic issues after the November update. From Desktop Mode to AOD, Lock screen, and notification drawers, a lot of basic Pixel features don’t work as they should. A larger pool of users are witnessing accidental touches and unresponsive cameras. It’s not uncommon for new Pixel updates to introduce more problems than new features. We’ve been seeing a similar phenomenon for almost a year, and I’ve lamented about it to no avail. Google has admitted that nearly 75% of all internal code is written by AI, and that appears to be affecting yet another round of updates released this week. The recent November 2026 Pixel Drop that brought a host of AI features, especially to the Pixel 10 series, and supposedly dozens of bug fixes also appears to be causing a wide range of sporadic issues for Pixel owners. We’ve come across several reports on Reddit, suggesting users are struggling with unexplained issues since the update.

title: Google Messages’ big search redesign is now rolling out to beta testers
summary: Finding old texts, photos, and links is getting easier.
body: TL;DR Google Messages’ redesigned search interface is starting to appear on some of our devices running the beta version. The new interface organizes shared images, videos, and links into visual sections, with a bottom search field and separate results for chats and messages. A new in-chat search shortcut is also appearing for some beta testers. Google Messages is getting serious about making old conversations and shared content easier to find. After months of spotting search improvements hidden in the app’s code, we’re finally seeing some of those changes arrive on actual devices. Back in September, we uncovered a major Google Messages search overhaul that promised to make finding photos, videos, links, and individual messages considerably easier. At the time, we had to manually enable the redesigned interface. That’s no longer necessary.

title: The Pixel Journal app now lets you record and add audio via Recorder

body: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR Google’s Journal app has now gained functional Recorder app integration. This integration allows you to make new audio recordings or add existing ones to your journal entry. The integration is rolling out now via Google’s Journal and Recorder apps. Google’s Journal app recently gained an update that paved the way for integration with the Pixel Recorder app . More specifically, the app received a “Record new audio” button. This button prompted users to update the Pixel Recorder app, but there wasn’t actually a pending update at the time. Fortunately, it looks like this Recorder integration is live now. APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship. We updated to recent versions of the Journal (v2026.10.27) and Recorder apps (v4.2.20261001) and discovered that we can now use the “Record new audio” option in the Journal app. Furthermore, there’s also an “Add existing recording” button so you can add a previous audio recording. title: Google Sheets now lets others explore your data without accessing your spreadsheet
summary: Let your data do the talking, without revealing everything else.
body: TL;DR Google Sheets now lets users publish Gemini-powered Canvas dashboards, calendars, and task boards through shareable links. People can interact with a published Canvas without accessing or editing the original spreadsheet. Users can control who sees the Canvas and choose whether it updates automatically when spreadsheet data changes. Google Sheets is great for organizing information, but sharing it with others isn’t always convenient. Say you’re managing a project with multiple deadlines and tasks. You might have everything organized in a spreadsheet, but no one wants to scroll through dozens of rows just to see what’s happening next. Google already has a feature called Canvas that uses Gemini to turn spreadsheet data into interactive dashboards, calendars, and task boards. Now, it’s making these creations easier to share by giving them their own links, without requiring access to the original spreadsheet.

body: TL;DR Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of NVIDIA. The move follows two scandals: an affair with a foreign intelligence agent and one with a direct NVIDIA report. CFO Colette Kress has been appointed interim CEO as the board searches for a replacement. In a move that has seemed inevitable for the past few days, Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of NVIDIA, according to a statement from the company . The decision was announced by NVIDIA’s board of directors who appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. Kress will serve in both roles until NVIDIA appoints a permanent replacement CEO.
